Independent Hermitian-plane, dual conic/pencil, and normalization calculations
correctness.rationale: Hermitian polarity is nondegenerate and sends an isotropic point to its distinct tangent. The orthogonal plane to an isotropic point has that line as radical and anisotropic one-dimensional quotient; the orthogonal plane to an external point is a nondegenerate Hermitian plane, with q+1 isotropic points by the norm map. Thus all external quadratic-field points are ordinary crossings and there are no other intersections. Frobenius fixes the duals of the q+1 points on the subfield conic (odd characteristic) or subfield line (even characteristic); q² external subfield points are crossings. In odd characteristic the dual points lie on a nonsingular conic, so every pair gives a distinct rational intersection and no third rational line passes there. In even characteristic the pencil center is [1:1:1], external because 1+1+1=1; the full pencil covers the rational plane and has a unique line through any other point. The normalization is the disjoint union of the lines with the indicated descent. For odd extensions subtract q(q+1) rational preimages over crossings and add q² crossing images, including those with no rational branch. For even extensions subtract qE. Substituting these counts into the logarithmic definition gives the displayed exponents and coverages at m=1,2. The finite q=2,3 examples are not used as proof of generality.
residual_risks: The formula is for the specified descent of the entire reduced union, not for an arbitrary twist, a subarrangement, or the smooth Hermitian curve.

value.rationale: This is the canonical complete tangent arrangement of a classical unital, with a concrete subfield descent rather than a selected slice. Its zeta function records every extension count; the rational branch spectrum separates two normalization splitting patterns which the common geometric crossing multiplicity alone cannot reveal. The exact data are useful for arithmetic comparison with other singular arrangements and clarify why odd-extension counts require adding crossings with zero rational preimages.
residual_risks: The zeta calculation is short once the arithmetic incidences are known, and the classical geometric inputs are not new. No general claim about zeta functions of arbitrary unitals or arrangements is made.
